survivingClaim: MEASURED (not interval-certified): Z_{Gamma(2)}(s, chi_{a,b}) has a real off-line zero at 0.95033 for (0.01,0.02), 0.83990 for (0.03,0.05), 0.72661 for (0.02,0.07); none on [0.505,1] for (0.05,0.12). The object has an Euler product over geodesics and an s <-> 1-s equation with elementary factor; it lacks the integers, order one, finite degree and zeta's sign of the zero side. PROVED: any non-negative-coefficient series c Z'/Z + E with the PSL2(Z) Selberg zeta has sigma* >= 1/2 > beta/2 (Maass pole at 1/2 + 9.5337i plus Landau), so Theorem PC is silent at rho/2; the pole-cancelling difference has disjoint supports; in Z'/Z - 2 zeta'/zeta(2s) the rho/2 poles cancel.
obstruction: Selberg zetas do not supply the missing control: the s <-> 1-s equation belongs to the order-2 function, while the degree-one unimodular Ruelle product has poles where Z has zeros, so every Landau-positivity mechanism holds with reversed inequality. Its off-line zeros are real and finitely many, so it tests nothing at height > 0. The Selberg companion for Theorem PC is closed: sigma* >= 1/2.

lesson: What separates zeta from the Selberg family is the integers (additive structure), order one and the sign of the zero side; filter new attacks on those. Do not re-attempt Selberg companions for Theorem PC.
